Summary: This bill would require the Commissioner of the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) to develop materials to inform the public about options for obtaining doula care, including information about State laws regarding access by a doula to hospital spaces and Medicaid reimbursement for doula services. The bill would also require such Commissioner to develop a submission form to receive feedback from doulas working with birthing parents in hospitals in New York City and to share a summary of the feedback annually. Finally, the bill would establish a doula advisory council to study the work of doulas in the city and advise the Citywide Doula Program, comprised of doulas, advocates for birthing people, a DOHMH appointee, and, upon invitation, a representative of NYC Health + Hospitals. The doula advisory council would meet 3 times annually and disband after 6 such meetings and after submitting a report of its findings and recommendations to the Mayor and to the Speaker and posting the report on the DOHMH website.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to creating resources for access to doulas and a doula advisory council

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subdivision d of section 17-199.10 of the administrative code of the city of New York is redesignated subdivision f.
§ 2. Section 17-199.10 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding new subdivisions d and e to read as follows:
d. Doula-related information. No later than July 1, 2027, the commissioner shall develop materials to inform the public about options for obtaining doula care and the parameters of such care, including, but not limited to, provisions of the public health and social services laws regarding access by a doula to hospital spaces and Medicaid reimbursement for doula services. The commissioner shall post such materials on the department’s website and share such materials with the citywide doula program and the health and hospitals corporation.
e. Doula feedback. No later than December 31, 2027, the commissioner shall make available and maintain on the department’s website a publicly accessible form to receive feedback from doulas practicing in the city regarding their experiences working with birthing people in hospitals in the city.
§ 3. Paragraph 3 of subdivision f of section 17-199.10 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 170 for the year 2025 and as redesignated by section one of this local law, is amended to read as follows: 
3. Any updated information regarding implementation of the plan required by subdivision b of this section since the prior annual report; [and]
§ 4. Subparagraph (k) of paragraph 4 of subdivision f of section 17-199.10 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 170 for the year 2025 and as redesignated by section one of this local law, is amended to read as follows: 
(k) An analysis of the use and outcomes of the citywide doula program[.]; and
§ 5. Subdivision f of section 17-199.10 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as redesignated by section one of this local law, is amended by adding a new paragraph 5 to read as follows:
5. Beginning with the report due June 30, 2028, a summary of feedback received pursuant to subdivision e of this section.
§ 6. Doula advisory council established. a. Definition. For purposes of this section, the term “city” means the city of New York.
b. Doula advisory council. The department of health and mental hygiene shall establish and maintain a doula advisory council.
1. Purpose. The doula advisory council shall study doula services in the city and advise the citywide doula program established pursuant to subdivision c of section 17-199.10 of the administrative code of the city of New York regarding best practices to support doulas and birthing people using doulas. 
2. Composition. The doula advisory council shall be composed of the following individuals:
(a) One member appointed by the commissioner of health and mental hygiene, who shall serve as chair;
(b) Two members from organizations that represent the interests of birthing people, as determined and appointed by the commissioner of health and mental hygiene;
(c) Two doulas working in the city appointed by the speaker of the council; and
(d) Upon acceptance of an invitation from the commissioner of health and mental hygiene, a representative of the New York city health and hospitals corporation.
3. Invitations. The chair may invite members of the public and representatives of relevant federal, state, and local agencies and authorities to participate in the work of the doula advisory council.
4. Terms. Each member of the doula advisory council shall serve at the pleasure of the officer who appointed the member. In the event of a vacancy on the advisory council, a successor shall be appointed in the same manner as the original appointment for the remainder of the unexpired term. All members of the doula advisory council shall serve without compensation.
5. Appointments. All appointments required by this section shall be made no later than 120 days after a vacancy.
6. Meetings. The chair shall convene the first meeting of the doula advisory council no later than 30 days after the last member has been appointed, except that where an initial appointment of a member of the doula advisory council has not been made, the chair shall convene the first meeting of the doula advisory council after the establishment of a quorum. The doula advisory council shall meet not less than 3 times per year.
7. Expiration. The doula advisory council shall be disbanded no later than 180 days after meeting 6 times pursuant to paragraph 6 of this subdivision and submitting the report required pursuant to subdivision d of this section.
c. Information. The department of health and mental hygiene shall provide the annual summary required pursuant to subdivision e of section 17-199.10 of the administrative code to the doula advisory council each year, until such council expires and is disbanded. 
d. Report. No later than 180 days after its final meeting, the doula advisory council shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council summarizing its studies of doula services in the city, any recommendations to the department of health and mental hygiene regarding the citywide doula program, and any recommended best practices to support doulas and birthing people using doulas in the city. Such report shall also be posted on the website of the department of health and mental hygiene. 
§ 7. This local law takes effect immediately.
